ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 3 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Booker T. Washington

code.originalText: Three-week check after losartan titration and dapagliflozin start

text.paragraph: Three-week check after the losartan increase and dapagliflozin start. [S]

Mr. Washington returns three weeks after losartan was increased to 100 mg and dapagliflozin started. His home readings now run in the 140s and 150s over 90s. He has had no headaches for two weeks and palpitations are rare. He passes a little more urine in the daytime since starting dapagliflozin but has had no genital itching, thirst, or lightheadedness on standing. He has taken no pain relievers. On two trips he ate restaurant meals most days and has begun asking for dishes without added salt. [S]

list.item:
Severe hypertension with hypertensive kidney disease, improving (I12.9). Blood pressure 148/92 mmHg on full doses of amlodipine and losartan, still above target. [S]
Start chlorthalidone 12.5 mg daily as the third agent; potassium at the upper end of normal also favors a thiazide-like diuretic.
The sick-day rule now includes chlorthalidone.

Chronic kidney disease stage G3b A3 (N18.32). Creatinine 2.4 mg/dL (up 14 percent from 2.1) and eGFR 30 (down 17 percent from 36), the expected early dip from losartan and dapagliflozin and within the 30 percent accepted. Potassium 4.9 mmol/L, bicarbonate 22. [S]
Continue losartan 100 mg and dapagliflozin 10 mg.
Potassium, sodium, and creatinine at the four-week check, with a urine albumin-creatinine ratio.
